skill.name: config-auditing
skill.description: Audit Neovim configurations for structure, performance, security, deprecated APIs, and maintainability issues.
skill.summary: Reviews Neovim configuration health with checklists, best practices, and deprecated API guidance.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples for local Neovim auditing. I confirmed the unredacted secret-search command and added a semantic finding for headless checks that can execute the audited configuration. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Secret detection prints full credential values.
remediation.suggestion: Redact values in secret-search output and report only file, line, and key name unless the user explicitly requests full local details.

remediation.issue: Some health checks load or execute the audited Neovim configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these commands as optional, ask for confirmation first, and prefer static file inspection or --clean commands when full config execution is not required.

remediation.issue: The documentation does not clearly state the privacy scope of local command output.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid broad home-directory scans and to review command output for paths or secrets before sharing it.

semantic_findings.title: Unredacted Secret Disclosure in Audit Output
semantic_findings.description: The secret-detection example searches for API keys, tokens, passwords, and secrets, but it prints the full matching assignment. An audit run could expose real credential values to the agent transcript.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The grep expression targets secret-like assignments and has no redaction step. The surrounding section confirms the intent is exposed credential detection.

semantic_findings.title: Audit Commands Execute User Neovim Configuration
semantic_findings.description: Several checks start Neovim headlessly or explicitly load init.lua. If the audited configuration is untrusted, those commands can execute arbitrary Lua or plugin startup code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands invoke Neovim in modes that can load configuration code, and one command directly dofiles init.lua. This is expected for diagnostics but risky for untrusted configs.

content.value_statement: Neovim setups can accumulate deprecated APIs, slow startup paths, and unsafe settings over time. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured audit with clear findings and fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guides audits of Neovim structure, performance, security, compatibility, and redundancy.
Provides detection patterns for deprecated and removed Neovim APIs.
Explains lazy.nvim plugin specification, trigger, and dependency best practices.
Reviews option, keymap, autocmd, and directory layout patterns.
Produces graded audit reports with critical issues, warnings, suggestions, and statistics.
limitations: Requires access to the user's Neovim configuration files or command output.
Shell checks may need user approval and can expose local paths or secret values.
Deprecated API guidance depends on the user's installed Neovim version.
Does not automatically fix configuration files unless the user requests edits.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Personal Neovim Setup
use_cases.description: Review a large or aging configuration and identify structure, startup, and compatibility issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a Neovim Upgrade
use_cases.description: Check a configuration for APIs deprecated or removed in the target Neovim version.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Editor Configs
use_cases.description: Compare shared Neovim settings against maintainable lazy.nvim, keymap, and option patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Config Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of an existing setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Neovim configuration for structure, startup issues, deprecated APIs, and security concerns. Start with read-only checks and summarize the top fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deprecated APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Neovim config for APIs deprecated or removed in my installed Neovim version. Explain each issue and recommend the modern replacement.

prompt_templates.title: Improve lazy.nvim Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my lazy.nvim plugin setup for eager loading, missing triggers, dependency problems, and slow startup patterns. Prioritize changes by impact.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Security-Focused Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before sharing a config
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Neovim configuration for exposed secrets, unsafe shell commands, risky modeline or exrc settings, and plugin execution risks. Redact sensitive values in all output.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a general Neovim health check.
output: Overall grade with the detected Neovim version and config location.
Critical issues first, followed by warnings and suggestions.
Statistics such as Lua file count, plugin count, startup time, and deprecated API count.

output_examples.input: A user wants to upgrade to a newer Neovim release.
output: A compatibility summary for the target version.
Deprecated API matches with file and line references.

output_examples.input: A user asks why startup feels slow.
output: Likely eager-loaded plugins and heavy startup hooks.
Suggested lazy-loading triggers for commands, filetypes, events, or keys.
A short list of changes to test before larger refactors.

best_practices: Run read-only checks first and ask before executing commands that load the full config.
Redact secrets and private paths from audit output before sharing results.
Match deprecated API checks to the exact Neovim version under review.
anti_patterns: Running every shell example without confirming the user wants command execution.
Printing token, password, or API key values directly in audit output.
Treating optional style suggestions as critical runtime failures.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Neovim configuration structure, performance, security settings, deprecated APIs, redundancy, and common lazy.nvim practices.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it edit my Neovim files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides findings and recommendations unless you explicitly ask the agent to make file changes.

faq.question: Why does it need command examples?
faq.answer: Some checks need local Neovim version, startup, plugin, or file information that is easiest to collect with shell commands.

faq.question: Can it detect deprecated APIs for every Neovim version?
faq.answer: It covers documented patterns in the skill files and should be matched against the user's installed Neovim version.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled during an audit?
faq.answer: Secret values should be redacted. The audit should report locations and key names without exposing the actual values.
